summary:
I MAY HAVE JUST FOUND SOME INSANE LORE,

The same guy who gave Bitcoin its iconic orange logo also created a Bitcoin cat in 2010 and somehow almost everyone forgot about it

On November 1, 2010, BitcoinTalk user bitboy posted Bitcoin Maneki Neko, a Bitcoin version of the Japanese lucky cat. He specifically told early Bitcoin users they could use it as a “good luck charm for your commerce website,” provided left- and right-paw versions, and later placed the artwork in the public domain

What makes this way crazier is who bitboy was.
Earlier that exact same day, he posted the Bitcoin graphics package that introduced the flat orange Bitcoin design that evolved into the logo we all recognize today. Bitcoin Design credits his version with the orange #F7931A color and the tilted Bitcoin symbol that remains ubiquitous. 

 Bitboy’s original Bitcoin logo thread

 Bitcoin Design — history of the logo

So on the same day in 2010, one artist helped create Bitcoin’s most recognizable visual identity and gave Bitcoin its own lucky cat.

And people actually cared about the cat at the time.

This cat has some insane lore and has yet to see the light on Solana - Paired to BTC

$Neko - The Bitcoin Cat

summary:
Fly Rebase, $FLYR, is a rebase protocol on Robinhood Chain, launching through pons_v2 at 10:00 UTC.

The contract stores shares, not balances. Your visible balance is shares held times one global coefficient. A rebase rewrites that single coefficient, so every wallet moves by the identical factor at the same moment. Nothing is minted to anyone, nothing is taken from anyone, and your proportional share of supply cannot change by construction.

It is not yield and not an emission. It is a rescale. The invariant quantity is the ratio, and the ratio does not move.

The project is built alongside fruitflydev, whose FLYBRAIN work runs a real fruit fly connectome, 165,122 neurons and 10,228,000 synaptic connections traced by electron microscopy. That science is theirs and stays credited to them. Fly Rebase contributes the supply mechanism: fixed structure, elastic magnitude, the same separation the connectome demonstrates.

Contract address posted on X and on the site at launch. Nowhere else.

Fixed structure. Elastic magnitude.
